newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Seguin says candidate to lead Gaullists.
newsitem.headline: France's Seguin says candidate to lead Gaullists.

text.p: Former National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin announced on Thursday he was a candidate to take over the leadership of France's Gaullist RPR party from defeated prime minister Alain Juppe after the left's election win.

Seguin, who led the French referendum campaign against the Maastricht treaty on European union in 1992, said in a statement he would also stand for parliamentary floor leader of the party founded by President Jacques Chirac.

Juppe has been under pressure to resign as president of the Rally for the Republic Party in favour of Seguin after the disastrous loss in Sunday's National Assembly election to new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.

Seguin, 54, said he would be a candidate to lead the RPR parliamentary group for an interim period when the caucus elects its officers next Tuesday. "He also expressed the wish for the creation of an executive representing all wings of the group for that period," the statement said.
Juppe has said he will call an emergency party congress for September to elect a new leader but failed to spell out if he would be a candidate.
Acting RPR secretary-general Jean-Louis Debre said on Thursday that he hoped the congress could be brought forward to July to end the bitter feuding.
